continuity_scope: Television-adaptation continuity, restricted to Season 1 Episode 1, "Chosen: Part 1" (MTV original episode witness). This pass excludes Terry Brooks's novels, games, later episodes/seasons, and other adaptations.

work_or_witnesses.edition: Season 1 Episode 1, "Chosen: Part 1"; MTV original broadcast witness

coverage_rule: Include named individual dramatic characters who materially act in the primary Episode 1 witness and provide the opening story's distinct roles: Amberle, Wil Ohmsford, Eretria, Allanon, and King Eventine. Peoples/species, magic, Ellcrys/Forbidding concepts, artifacts, places, orders, titles, and post-apocalyptic history are terms, not nodes.
omissions: All unnamed Chosen, Rovers, demons, palace personnel, and other collectives.
Characters first materially established after Episode 1, and all later episode/season development.
Peoples/species, magic, Ellcrys and Forbidding concepts, Elfstones, places, orders, titles, and post-apocalyptic history as character nodes.
Terry Brooks novels, games, and other adaptation continuity.
content_cautions: Elf, human, and Rover are fictional source terms; no real race, ethnicity, nationality, disability/body, or cultural equivalence is made.

The selected primary episode includes danger, threatened death, and youth-coded characters. No age, violence/trauma, disability/body, sexuality, ethnicity, or real-world cultural classification is inferred.
The television adaptation is treated as its own witness; no book detail or later reveal corrects or expands its Episode 1 record.
uncertainties: The public MTV archive no longer exposes a full transcript. Claims are restricted to directly observable Episode 1 actions with scene/time locators and marked primary-text.
No individual relationship, identity, or outcome claim is added when it depends on Part 2 or later episodes.
evidence_basis: The primary MTV Episode 1 witness establishes all narrative claims. The official MTV series locator identifies the television program; performer credits are not used as ontology evidence. No fan wiki or Wikipedia was used.
